top5.why: This pool variant drops the onlyFactoryOwner modifier, so anyone could drain protocol fees if this variant is the deployed one.
Missing onlyFactoryOwner lets anyone change the protocol fee split.
Standard Uniswap V3 factory logic; checked for deviations and found none.
Permissionless but the fees only go to feeReceiver, so low impact.
Core pool matches canonical Uniswap V3 token-for-token, so no defect found.
Share price comes from strategy balance, so a first-depositor donation can round later depositors' shares to zero.
Shares are burned before the strategy pays, and the strategy pays min(balance, amount), so users can lose value.
balanceOfY subtracts the x vault's totalSupply and can revert, freezing Y vault accounting and withdrawals.
Governance can set an impl that is delegatecalled with strategy storage and funds (trust risk).
Fee and payout logic relies on x or y caller identity and withdraws a computed fraction of deposited funds.
Uses latestAnswer with no staleness check, but this is Aave's standard design.
Gated by the ACL manager for asset-listing or pool admins.
Admin-gated.
Admin-only upgrade path; stock Aave code.
Guarded by an implementation-is-zero check, so it cannot be re-initialized.
Matches canonical Permit2: nonce consumed, signature verified, spender bound to msg.sender.
Nonce is checked and incremented; the signature binds owner, spender and deadline.
Allowance and expiration are enforced correctly.
Rejects the zero-address signer and supports EIP-1271 for contract signers.
The witness type string is concatenated into the type hash, which is the standard design.
Balance is decremented before transfer, so it is safe.
Standard allowance logic with a max-allowance bypass.
Plain mint of balance against msg.value.
Standard ERC20 approve.
Delegates to transferFrom as in the canonical contract.
Forwards user-controlled calldata to a fixed set of marketplaces; the router holds no persistent funds.
isNotLocked and the lockedBy sender mapping match the canonical Universal Router.
Callback caller is verified against the computed pool address.
Callable by anyone, but only approves fixed OpenSea and Sudoswap spenders.
Permissionless call to a fixed distributor, with rewards sent to a fixed address.
The pair and tokens are never validated, so a fake pair can claim inflated amounts and refunds are paid out of any token balance the migrator holds.
Anyone can sweep tokens left in the router; this is standard design and relies on multicall atomicity.
Anyone can unwrap WETH held by the router.
Fee-bips handling in a payments helper that can be misused only if tokens are left behind.
Pool address is verified through CallbackValidation, so it looks sound.

The caller-supplied modifyCalldata is run through the position manager multicall by the factory, which owns every launch's LP NFT, so an attacker can decrease liquidity on other launches' positions and take the tokens.
Caller-supplied preCommands and preInputs run on the Universal Router under the factory's token approvals and balances.
Permissionless; its fee accounting uses balance deltas, and it reverts if pushDistribute reverts.
Loops over an unbounded holder list and transfers to each, so an attacker can bloat the list or use a reverting recipient to freeze fee harvests.
Leaves max-expiry Permit2 approvals to the router with leftover allowances.
